messages:
Lina (PM): quick check — we need to decide how to slice next quarter bandwidth across three major asks: 1) FinCorp private compliance bundle (sales-led), 2) routing/telemetry improvements for 95th p99 latency observability, 3) autoscaling primitives for Dedicated. thinking about a 'bandwidth slices' approach instead of single RICE ordering. :thinking:
Sam (Eng): can you sketch what you mean by slices? is this a capacity reserve or prioritization per sprint?
Lina (PM): both — idea is reserve X% runway for customer-driven fastpaths, Y% for infra/platform runway, Z% for experiments. avoids single-threaded backlogs. example proposal: 50/30/20 (customer/infra/experiments).
Ana (Product Ops): I like it for predictability. sales already promised FinCorp an ETA if we can do a scoped compliance deliverable (minimal controls + audit logs). they asked for end-of-q2.
Michael (Eng-Infra): we have hiring freeze for infra until headcount req approved; 30% might be optimistic. autoscaling work touches runtime kernels and infra scheduling — that's 2 strong engs for 2 sprints minimal spike.
Sam (Eng): autoscaling also requires infra infra changes + e2e tests. if we slice 50% to FinCorp and we only have 20% for infra, autoscale gets blocked. we need to sequence: spike -> canary -> rollout.
Priya (Dir Product): what about mixing frameworks — use RICE to pick what to build inside each slice. e.g., customer slice sorted by impact, infra slice sorted by effort to unblock roadmap. this avoids mixing apples and oranges.
Lina (PM): exactly. here's a quick scoring I put together for the top items (very rough):
```
FinCorp compliance: Reach 8, Impact 9, Confidence 6, Effort 5 -> RICE ~ (8*9*6)/5 = 86
Autoscale primitives: Reach 6, Impact 8, Confidence 5, Effort 8 -> RICE ~ 30
Routing telemetry: Reach 7, Impact 7, Confidence 7, Effort 4 -> RICE ~ 86
```
Lina (PM): so FinCorp and telemetry tie-ish by RICE, but telemetry is infra-heavy and unlocks multiple customers; FinCorp is revenue-backed and timeboxed.
Ana (Product Ops): sales says FinCorp contract has a revenue milestone tied to delivery. that's non-trivial if we slip.
Sam (Eng): proposal: run a 2-week infra spike for autoscale (1 eng) funded from experiments slice, reserve a fastpath for FinCorp as 2-week scoped deliverable that can fall back to hosted-only (no private on-prem) if needed. telemetry gets the next sprint window and a smaller scoped MVP.
Priya (Dir Product): that sounds practical. can we commit to numbers? Lina -> plz put proposed % split in roadmap doc and we'll sign off in triage.
Lina (PM): propose split: 45% FinCorp (customer commits + will take some product hours), 25% infra (autoscale spike + tests), 30% telemetry (MVP + followups). leaves room for canary/rollback.
Michael (Eng-Infra): with 25% we can do the spike but not full autoscale. we should include a gating checklist: kernel perf test, kv-cache behavior, canary policy.
Sam (Eng): I'll estimate implementation tasks and update the product board by EOD. Lina can you add the FinCorp fallbacks (hosted-only + audit-log export) so scope is clear?
Lina (PM): will do. also adding a short decision rubric: if infra estimate > 3 sprints -> downgrade autoscale to phase 1 (observability + manual scale ops) and reallocate 10% to experiments.
Ana (Product Ops): calendar note: sales sync with FinCorp on Thursday, flagged as delivery dependency.
deploy-bot: Reminder — roadmap sync scheduled Thu 11:00 for product + eng.
Priya (Dir Product): decision: run spike + scoped FinCorp delivery. Lina to capture in roadmap and we'll re-evaluate after spike. :thumbsup:
